key_insight: Magnetism controls ordering in Fe-rich Fe–Si alloys: D0₃ ordering dominates in the fully ordered ferromagnetic state, while paramagnetism promotes B2 ordering at elevated temperatures.
engineering_relevance: Linking magnetic state to atomic ordering can guide Fe–Si alloy design and thermal processing where ordering affects magnetic properties and mechanical behavior.
method: Calculate effective cluster interactions using density functional theory.
Resolve how magnetic state, lattice expansion, and Si concentration alter interactions.
Use Monte Carlo simulations to predict temperature-dependent ordering and phase equilibria.
evidence_signal: For bcc Fe–Si alloys containing up to 20 at% Si, the simulations reproduce experimentally observed phase equilibria and short-range order characteristics.
watch_item: Applicability beyond bcc alloys with up to 20 at% Si is not established by the abstract.
paper_title: First-principles modeling of ordering in Fe-rich Fe-Si alloys
